thread_analysis.thread_summary: Seiko Solutions (contact Yuko Kawabata) consults Allion (Masaya Iida, with technical answers drafted by Itsuo Sakai) about repurposing an existing Bluetooth Core Specification v4.2-based registration (a device previously sold under NTT Docomo's brand) under their own company name and product model, including questions about the spec's deprecation timeline and a general framework for assessing future registration feasibility.
all_questions_found: Can a v4.2-based registration with a changed seller/model still proceed after the spec's deprecation date? (see thread_0252_case_01)
What are the general conditions that determine whether a new registration is or isn't possible? (see thread_0252_case_02)
thread_analysis.key_technical_discussion: Core Specification deprecation timelines have two distinct milestones (Deprecated, then later Withdrawn) with only the latter actually blocking new registrations; registration feasibility for any future hardware combination reduces to four checkable conditions (existing QDID/DN registration, non-Withdrawn status, compatible Core Specification, no fatal cross-layer inconsistency).
thread_analysis.key_decision_logic: Both answers favor providing the customer with a reusable evaluation framework (the Deprecated/Withdrawn distinction; the four-condition checklist) rather than one-off case-specific answers, anticipating the customer's stated need to evaluate multiple future candidate options.
thread_analysis.consulting_takeaway: When a customer signals they're evaluating multiple future options rather than just the one immediate question, proactively provide a reusable decision framework rather than only answering the specific question asked, anticipating their stated need to self-evaluate future candidates.
